subject: Next steps: POC scope & multilingual model roster for TransactNow pilot
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@transactnow.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Next steps: POC scope & multilingual model roster for TransactNow pilot

Hi Daniel / Mei —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed POC plan so we can align and get the pilot contract moving. I tried to keep this focused and actionable.

Recap (what you told us)
- Primary use case: transaction categorization + customer message intent routing for support channels (web + mobile).
- Volume: ~1.2M monthly messages; initial sample for POC: ~10k labeled queries (mix of EN/ES/JA).
- Priority languages: English (en), Spanish (es), Japanese (jp).
- Compliance: data residency for EU subset later; POC can run in Redwood hosted US region as long as sample data is synthetic/pseudonymized.

POC objectives & success criteria (proposed)
- Accuracy: intent classification macro-F1 >= 0.86 on the validation holdout; entity extraction F1 >= 0.78 for named entities used in routing.
- Latency: p95 inference end-to-end < 500ms for 1kqps test profile (with batching on).
- Reliability: no more than 1% error/timeout rate during sustained 30-minute stress window.
- Cost guardrail: token cost per request budgeted to < $0.002 for average 60-token responses.
- Multilingual parity: English baseline +/-5% for Spanish/Japanese on key intents.

Model roster (trial configuration)
- Primary (recommended for POC): Redwood-Open-FT-3B (open fine-tuned variant optimized for classification/NER).
- Fallback: Llama2-13B-Quant (quantized variant for higher-latency tolerance; will be used when primary capacity or latency SLO is at risk).
- Multilingual augment: use lightweight language-specific tokenizer and a small translation pre-step for Japanese if direct JP performance underperforms (>5% gap).

Ownership & next steps
- Sales / AE: Vivek (me) — commercial lead, contract/POC signoff.
- Solutions Engineer: Ben Carter — evaluation harness, load profile, measurement scripts.
- Customer Success: Marissa Cole — acceptance criteria owner, onboarding.

Ask from TransactNow (deliverables to start POC)
1) Shared sample: 10k queries (CSV) with labels/intent and data dictionary. Prefer pseudonymized or synthetic for now.
2) Security questionnaire -> we will provide SOC2 summary; please flag any additional evidence.
3) NDA/PO or SOW signoff to schedule Dedicated slot.

Proposed timeline
- Week 0: NDA/SOW signed + sample data upload
- Week 1: Redwood spins up trial instance, seed model, run smoke tests
- Weeks 2–3: Evaluation period (metrics collection, error analysis, tuning)
- Week 4: Acceptance review, go/no-go, and next steps for expansion

Can you confirm the sample delivery date and whether TransactNow needs us to use EU data locality even for the POC samples? If you’re fine with the plan I’ll have Ben drop a test harness checklist and Marissa will send the rubric to confirm acceptance thresholds.

Thanks — looking forward to moving fast.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
https://redwood.ai

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@transactnow.com>

Date: 2026-02-15T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: POC scope & multilingual model roster for TransactNow pilot

Vivek —

Thanks for the clear summary. This matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Languages: yes — EN/ES/JP. For Japanese we expect more variation and some mixed-language queries (JP + EN), so translation pre-step is acceptable if it helps.
2) Data residency: for the POC we can provide pseudonymized samples hosted on our side (we'll give you a limited shared folder link). If all goes well we'll require EU-hosted inference for production but not for the POC.
3) Timeline: 6-week internal window from SOW signoff is our preference (gives our ops time to review). That said, we can tolerate the 4-week compressed timeline if Redwood needs earlier feedback.

Deliverables we can deliver next week:
- 10k sample rows CSV with intent labels (we will remove PII).
- Data dictionary and annotation guidelines (attached).

Security/compliance asks:
- Please send SOC2 summary and if possible an encrypted transport for sample upload (SFTP or a pre-signed S3 link).

For the SOW/PO: Mei will own signature on our side — I’ve looped her in. We look forward to Ben’s test harness and Marissa’s rubric.

Best,
Daniel Park
Director of Product Operations, TransactNow

Hi Daniel / Mei —

Thanks — small note on acceptance criteria and measurement so we’re aligned before Ben starts the harness:

Evaluation rubric (Marissa's suggested baseline)
- Classification: macro-F1 measured on a 2k holdout; pass if >=0.86.
- Entity extraction: per-entity F1; pass if weighted F1 >=0.78.
- Latency: p95 measured across three runs at target qps (1k/s sim); pass if < 500ms.
- Regression guardrail: if any language drops > 7% from English baseline, we trigger a joint tuning block (max 1 calibration pass).
- Edge-case handling: for queries with <50 token context we expect >=95% routing correctness on top-3 predictions.

Ben: can you prepare the harness checklist that will include: input format, downstream scoring scripts, load profile, and the test notebook for reproducibility? Also include a flag to swap the fallback model (Llama2-13B-Quant) during the run so we can measure fallback behavior.

Mei / Daniel: once you upload the sample CSV to the Drive link Vivek shared (or send S3 presigned link), we’ll onboard it and run a smoke evaluation in 48 hours.

I’ll track acceptance and will set a one-hour acceptance review in week 4.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
